messages:
Nora (People Ops): Quick policy check  a new parent is going on unpaid parental leave but will still get a small monthly on-call stipend. They want to keep deferring $100 to their 401(k) from that stipend and are asking whether employer matching will also apply and how loan repayments and vesting behave during the leave. Any vendor gotchas?

Diego (SRE): For context, stipend is separate taxable line item (ONCALL_STIP). We pay it while they're on leave for on-call coverage. Curious whether match is based on 'company contributions per pay' or 'pay period compensation' for the plan.

Claire (Payroll): Short answer: matching follows the plan document and the recordkeepers interpretation of eligible compensation. In our implementation: if the stipend is coded as taxable wages (ONCALL_STIP) and the employee defers, that compensation is considered eligible for match calculations. So employer match should apply to the portion eligible under the employees deferral election.

Claire (Payroll): Important details and caveats:
- Payroll coding: ensure the stipend is entered as ONCALL_STIP (taxable earnings) before payroll cutoff.
- Match timing: our payroll exports employee deferrals and company match per pay date to the recordkeeper. The recordkeeper typically applies match on the same pay date if it receives the export. If payroll marks the period as "unpaid" but still has taxable earnings (the stipend), the export will include both employee deferral and employer match.
- Plan rules: some plans tie employer match to "compensation" defined in the SPD (e.g., base pay only, or exclude certain stipends). If the plan excludes stipends, the recordkeeper will not match. I will confirm whether our SPD explicitly includes ONCALL_STIP.

Nora (People Ops): What about vesting and loan repayments? If the match goes through while they're on leave, does vesting continue? And for a payroll-deducted loan payment, will deductions keep happening?

Claire (Payroll): Vesting: vesting is governed by plan schedule, not active pay. If we make employer contributions while they're on leave, those contributions follow the normal vesting schedule (i.e., contribution date is what matters). Being on unpaid leave does not automatically pause vesting unless plan language says otherwise.

Claire (Payroll): Loan repayments: these require active payroll deductions. If payroll cannot take regular post-tax loan payments because there are no wages in a period (stipend alone may be insufficient if employees election is to have loan payments spread across regular pay), you have options:
- If the stipend is sufficient and coded as wages, payroll can capture loan repayment from that line (requires manual setup and early ticket before cutoff).
- If payroll cannot capture it, the employee must make direct repayments to the recordkeeper; otherwise the loan may default and be treated as a distribution (taxable event). We should proactively surface this to the employee.

Diego (SRE): Anything about minimums? They worry a $100 deferral might be rejected. Also any cadence/aggregation issues if only one small payment is made in a pay period.

Claire (Payroll): Recordkeeper minimums: most recordkeepers accept small deferrals, but some plans or vendors have a $25 or $50 per-contribution minimum. Frequency/aggregation: if the recordkeeper receives a contribution file for that employee for the pay date, it will post it; odd-looking patterns are fine operationally but might trigger an inquiry during an audit. I'll confirm our vendors minimum contribution rules for our specific plan.

Carlos (Finance): Budget note: if match applies on stipends broadly, that increases matching liability slightly. If its limited to taxable wages as coded, we can estimate run rate. Happy to update forecast once Claire confirms.

Benefits Bot: Added reference: benefits.plan.docs/401k-spd (internal) and benefits.hr.kb/stipend-leave-qa.

Claire (Payroll): Action items: 1) I'll check the SPD and ping the recordkeeper to confirm whether ONCALL_STIP is treated as eligible compensation for matching and whether any per-contribution minimums apply. 2) I'll confirm the export timing and loan repayment behavior for single-line stipend deductions. 3) Draft KB blurb for managers/new hires: "Stipends, matching, and leave  how to keep deferring and what to watch for".

Nora (People Ops): Thank you  please tag me when the KB draft is ready and share the recordkeeper response so we can advise the employee.

Claire (Payroll): Will do.

(End of thread)
